transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-07-13 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Owen (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Hearthwell Head of ML), Daniel Kim (Platform), Lena Ortiz (Security)

Summary (auto): quick check-in for renewal options, EU sovereignty concerns, and onprem pilot logistics.

[00:00] Maya: thanks everyone for jumping on, I'll run us through the agenda. We're here to align on the renewal numbers and the EU onprem pilot in frankfurt, and make sure security items are covered.
[00:22] Priya: thanks, yeah we wanted to double-check pricing tiers, specifically how committed capacity vs burst works. Our usage spiked last month during a training rollout and we saw higher token spend.
[00:35] Owen: right, so two levers — dedicated reserved pools for predictable throughput, or hosted with burst credits. For your production latency targets (sub-150ms p50 for the customer-facing routes) we recommend a small dedicated pool plus autoscale buffer. The math we ran suggests ~40% uplift over current baseline.
[00:56] Daniel: that 40% number, is that assuming default batching? We use shorter sequences but high concurrency. We don't want to overpay for heavy quantization that might regress answers.
[01:10] Owen: it's workload-aware. We profiled your traces; because you have many short requests, continuous batching helps but the per-token cost is sensitive to batch size. Quantization (8-bit/4-bit) can reduce GPU memory and costs but there's a risk to tail-case completions — we can run a prompt-regression eval if you want.
[01:35] Priya: yes please, we need a quality baseline. Also, can you confirm private deployment options for EU? Our legal team requires data at rest to stay in EU and keys under our control.
[01:50] Maya: understood. For Sovereignty we can do Redwood Private in a customer VPC or onprem package. KMS integration is supported, both customer-managed keys (BYOK) and Redwood-managed with strict key access controls. We'll send the KMS integration matrix after this call.
[02:05] Lena: from security side we need SOC2 Type II reports, audit log retention, and confirmation on HSM usage if we bring our own key. Also want to understand how telemetry is stored and whether logs ever traverse non-EU regions during failover.
[02:23] Owen: good question. For Private, control plane metadata stays in the customer-controlled network. There are a couple of nuances: automated failover can route requests to a compatible EU region variant if the primary is unhealthy; we can pin the deployment to a geo to avoid routing outside EU if that's a hard requirement. I'll put that in writing.
[02:45] Priya: pinning sounds safer; what's the SLA implication? If we pin and a region goes down, do we accept reduced availability?
[02:55] Maya: yes. There are three routing policies: latency-first, cost-first, and geo-pinned. Geo-pinned preserves residency but reduces cross-region failover. We can include a canary failover window in the SOW so we simulate a controlled failover during the pilot.
[03:18] Daniel: about the onprem pilot — we have a small rack in frankfurt we can use. What's the minimum hardware footprint Redwood expects?
[03:30] Owen: minimal: 2x A100-equivalent GPUs recommended for a smoke-level pilot, 4x for realistic throughput. The runtime supports quantized models; we can start with a 2-GPU pilot to validate control plane, KV cache persistence and prefix caching — apologies, I said prefix 'cashing' earlier in the doc — prefix cache. We also need the nodes to have kernel-level optimizations enabled (hugepages, nvidia driver >= 525).
[03:58] Priya: we can do 2 GPUs initially. Are there networking requirements? We need to confirm outbound control plane egress.
[04:06] Owen: control plane egress is limited; the runtime opens an egress to the Redwood control plane for telemetry and orchestration. For air-gap or very strict environments we provide a Private control plane option that runs in your VPC. For fully air-gapped, there is an onprem package but it's a longer onboarding.
[04:26] Lena: do you support SAML/SSO? Our auditors require SSO and RBAC integration before we move to production.
[04:33] Maya: yes SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning are supported, as is role-based access. We'll include the IdP integration guide in the security pack.
[04:43] Priya: regarding the stress test, can you mimic our traffic spike profile? We have a 2-hour window that creates lots of small concurrent requests.
[04:52] Owen: absolutely. If you share the traffic trace we'll replay it in our harness; we can do a 48hr run to look at throughput stability, latency percentiles, and KV cache hit ratios. We can also run a canary failover during that window to validate geo-pinning behavior.
[05:10] Daniel: one more — how does billing change if we move to dedicated? Do we keep per-token overage or are bursts deducted differently?
[05:19] Maya: dedicated comes with committed baseline and burst pool pricing. Overage beyond burst is billed at a discounted overage rate compared to hosted. We'll put three options in the SOW: baseline commit (12 months), baseline + burst credits, and baseline with onprem pilot discount.
[05:34] Priya: timeline — we plan to sign an amendment by end of July if the pilot looks good. Our CFO needs the numbers and the legal team needs the KMS and SOC artifacts.
[05:45] Maya: sounds reasonable. We'll aim to deliver the SOW and security pack this week.
[05:50] Lena: small nit — we need to confirm where audit logs are stored and retention windows. Our default is 7 years for certain logs.
[06:00] Owen: we can configure long-term retention to your storage (S3 in EU) for logs; for Private deployments audit logs can be pushed to your bucket. I'll document exact retention hooks.
[06:12] Priya: any blockers from your side for the onprem pilot?
[06:16] Owen: just network access and GPU nodes. Once we get VPN and firewall windows we can provision the control plane link and deploy the runtime. We typically need 48 hours to spin up and validate connectivity.
[06:29] Maya: recap — Redwood to share SOW, security pack, and schedule stress-test. Customer to open network window, share traces, and provide list of audit requirements.
[06:42] Priya: agreed. Also, can you send a short one-page summary of the quantization tradeoffs so our ML folks can review?
[06:50] Owen: will do; I'll also include a short prompt-regression checklist.
[06:56] Daniel: on the contract side, any flexibility on start date for committed capacity? We might want the committed billing to start after the successful pilot.
[07:05] Maya: yes we can align start date to go-live post-pilot. We'll call that out in the amendment.
[07:12] Lena: thanks everyone. One last question — competitor risk. We are also talking to BigCloud AI about a managed endpoint; their default SLA looks similar but their residency controls are weaker.
[07:26] Maya: noted. We'll make sure the SOW and the security pack clarify the residency guarantees and the BYOK path.
[07:33] Priya: okay thanks, that's helpful.
[07:36] Maya: great. Next steps and owners will be in the follow-up email. Thanks all.

End transcript.
